title: Investigation of process factors and the positive and negative effects of outpatient psychotherapy using routine outcome monitoring
summary:
The overarching goal of the project is to investigate treatment processes and outcomes in routine outpatient care for patients with mental illnesses.
Specifically, the project has two objectives:
1) Previous studies have shown that it can have a positive effect on treatment outcomes when therapists receive regular, standardized feedback throughout the course of therapy regarding how their patients assess their current well-being and progress in therapy. This feedback is based on the results of short questionnaires that patients complete after each therapy session. The main objective of our study is to investigate whether this newly developed form of feedback has a positive effect on the further course and outcomes of treatment. To this end, participants and therapists receive regular feedback on randomly selected therapy sessions regarding how their patients assess the therapeutic relationship after the sessions and to what extent this assessment differs from their own. 
2) As a second objective of this study, we would like to examine in greater detail the course and outcomes of our outpatient treatments, using data that we collect from all patients for documentation and quality assurance purposes. In this context, we are interested, first, in how patients are doing at the end of treatment compared to the start of therapy; second, in how often positive as well as negative changes occur (e.g., in psychological distress and quality of life); third, in how satisfied patients are with the therapy; and fourth, in how they are doing after treatment is completed. We also want to examine how various parameters—which we collect as part of our quality assurance process after each therapy session—correlate with therapy outcomes. These parameters relate, for example, to how patients experience the therapeutic work with their therapist and what experiences they have had between therapy sessions.
conditions: All mental disorders (Chapter F of the ICD-10)

interventions.name: Outpatient psychotherapy (TP, VT, or systemic therapy) with routine outcome monitoring and the option for therapists to view patients' questionnaire data.

Outpatient psychotherapy (TP, VT, or systemic therapy) with routine outcome monitoring and specific feedback for therapists regarding discrepancies between the patient’s and therapist’s alliance ratings.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Outpatient therapy at one of the two centers; consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years, no outpatient therapy, no informed consent for the study
